main_body: Round stone tower: a grey brick wall (rows 42-94) with a window and an arched door, under a large green conical shingle roof (rows 0-40) with a brown eave band
top_band: Green shingled roof slope, rows ~2-39 (light mint at the upper left, dark teal at the right), then a brown eave band at rows 40-41
evidence: Reading down the middle column: the roof is a large shingled slope that reads as a top surface, like the Beodeul house roofs. A 2-row brown eave band follows at rows 40-41 with a dark shadow row under it. Below that is the stone wall face. The wall itself is a flat front view, but the roof provides the visible top surface, as it does on the references. The window has a frame, a sill and a dark inner top edge. The door has a stone surround and inset planks. A tower without a roof slope would fail, but this one has it.

style.evidence: The roof carries about 5 greens with per-shingle highlights and dark teal row lines. The stone wall has individually shaded bricks in 3-4 greys plus mortar lines. The door has wood grain, iron bands and a gold knob. The window has a glass gradient, a flower box and a brown frame. Outlines are dark tinted tones (dark teal beside the roof, dark brown at the eave, dark purple-grey in the mortar), not black. Some wall areas are a bit flat in the light bricks, but overall it is comparable to the references in richness and craft.
